## Summary

Stripe reviews direct integrations for Managed Payments eligibility based on factors including business type and geography. The November 7, 2026 capture lists 37 merchant business locations and 76 eligible Product tax codes. Each sale through a Checkout Session or Payment Link must meet the product, distribution, and tax-code requirements. Customer coverage and ongoing account requirements apply separately.

## Account Eligibility

Use a direct integration with a business based in a supported location. Connect platforms, Express accounts, and accounts controlled by a platform are excluded. A listed business location or Product tax code alone does not establish Stripe approval.

### Supported business locations

The November 7, 2026 eligibility capture lists 37 entries (raw lines 22–68).

- **North America**: CA, US
- **Europe**: AT, BE, BG, CH, CY, CZ, DE, DK, EE, ES, FI, FR, GB, GR, HR, HU, IE, IT, LI, LT, LU, LV, MT, NL, NO, PL, PT, RO, SE, SI, SK
- **Asia Pacific**: AU, HK, JP, SG

The April 23, 2026 eligibility capture lists 38 entries, including Gibraltar (GI, raw lines 21–69). The November list otherwise matches April's. The [[source-stripe-managed-payments-changelog]] separately reports 39 countries, including Australia, at the April 22, 2026 general-availability milestone. The November [[source-stripe-managed-payments-tax-compliance]] capture still includes Gibraltar for cross-border sales to customers there. The eligibility snapshots give no effective date for the listing change or account-specific treatment for Gibraltar.

## Product Eligibility

For each Product sold through a Checkout Session or Payment Link, assign an eligible tax code on the Product in the Dashboard or through the API. Sell directly to customers, hold the necessary distribution rights and licences, and provide a fully automated digital product. Live human intervention such as one-to-one coaching disqualifies the service. If Stripe determines that a product is ineligible, stop using Managed Payments for that product and take responsibility for its indirect tax liability. The guide points to Stripe Tax as a separate option when a product appears ineligible.

Eligible categories include software (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, and downloads), video games, digital media, self-study and on-demand courses, and electronically supplied business and web services. Physical goods, professional services, and live in-person events are excluded. Some Digital Audio Visual Works rows cover live-event content delivered as digital downloads, streams, or bundles (November raw lines 153–155 and 175–177, April raw lines 149–151 and 172–174). Check the exact code definition, direct sale, distribution rights, and automated delivery together. The general electronically supplied services description for `txcd_10000000` mentions minimal human involvement (line 108 in both captures). The fully automated Managed Payments requirement still applies.

### Exact eligible tax codes

Use the enumerated dated tables for code lookup: November 7 raw lines 104–183 (76 rows) and April 23 raw lines 104–180 (73 rows). The SaaS rows, for example, are `txcd_10103000`, `txcd_10103001`, `txcd_10103100`, and `txcd_10103101`. The personal and business distinctions on applicable codes matter for US sales.

November includes these four AIaaS rows (raw lines 117–120), which the November [[source-stripe-managed-payments-changelog]] capture dates to June 2, 2026.

| Tax code | AIaaS delivery and use |
| --- | --- |
| `txcd_10105001` | Cloud-based, personal use |
| `txcd_10105002` | Cloud-based, business use |
| `txcd_10105003` | Cloud-based and downloaded, personal use |
| `txcd_10105004` | Cloud-based and downloaded, business use |

April includes Website Advertising `txcd_10701000` (raw line 166) and November omits it. Website Hosting `txcd_10701100` remains in the November table. The April changelog capture listed Website Advertising in its September 22, 2025 one-time and in-app payment entry. The November changelog capture omits it from that entry. These omissions give no effective removal date, replacement code, or treatment of existing products or invoices.

November explicitly excludes data brokering from the four following information-service code definitions (raw lines 171–174). It also drops “of any kind” from the electronically delivered definitions.

| Tax code | Information service |
| --- | --- |
| `txcd_10701400` | Via website, business use |
| `txcd_10701401` | Via website, personal use |
| `txcd_10701410` | Electronically delivered, business use |
| `txcd_10701411` | Electronically delivered, personal use |

## Customer Coverage

Both captures describe coverage in more than 195 customer countries and territories. The nine listed restrictions are Ascension Island, China, Cuba, Iran, Kosovo, North Korea, Russia, Syria, and Tristan da Cunha. This customer coverage is distinct from merchant business locations and product eligibility.

## Ongoing Performance Requirements

Maintain a low historical dispute rate and have no prior risk issues. Stripe can issue refunds within 60 days of purchase in certain cases, including to help reduce chargebacks. Stripe applies regional cooling-off periods and other applicable consumer protection requirements.

payments-managed-payments-eligibility.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments/eligibility, November describes Stripe's eligibility review for direct integrations in supported business locations. Connect platforms, Express accounts and platform-controlled accounts are excluded (new raw lines 9-68). On a Checkout Session or Payment Link, each product must be an eligible fully automated digital sale direct to the customer, with distribution rights and an eligible Product tax code assigned in the Dashboard or via API. Physical goods, professional services and live in-person events are excluded. If Stripe finds the product ineligible, the merchant bears indirect tax liability and must stop using Managed Payments for that product (old raw lines 70-102 and new raw lines 70-102). More than 195 customer countries and territories and the nine restrictions are separate from merchant domicile. Ongoing eligibility requires a low historical dispute rate and no prior risk issues. Stripe can refund within 60 days in certain cases and applies applicable consumer protections (new raw lines 185-209). November omits Gibraltar and Website Advertising, adds four AIaaS codes and excludes data brokering from four information-service codes (old raw lines 30-62, 113-121 and 166-171; new raw lines 31-61, 117-120 and 170-174). The previous source-stripe-managed-payments-eligibility.md condensed April. The candidate restores Stripe's review, direct sales and distribution rights, and routes readers to the exact dated tax-code tables. A listed country and tax code are inputs to eligibility review and do not prove approval, compliant coverage or payment success.
payments-managed-payments-eligibility.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments/eligibility, the substantive listing changes are 38 to 37 merchant-location entries with Gibraltar omitted, four AIaaS additions txcd_10105001, txcd_10105002, txcd_10105003 and txcd_10105004 for cloud-only or downloaded-plus-cloud and personal or business use, removal of the Website Advertising row txcd_10701000, and new data-brokering exclusions for txcd_10701400, txcd_10701401, txcd_10701410 and txcd_10701411 (old raw lines 30-69, 113-121 and 166-171; new raw lines 31-68, 117-120 and 170-174). The changelog dates the AIaaS addition to June 2. The candidate preserves April's Gibraltar and Website Advertising entries and the changelog's separately dated 39-country April GA milestone in source-stripe-managed-payments-eligibility.md and proposes reciprocal concept wording and a changelog route. The November tax-compliance page's GI entry is for cross-border customer tax coverage. The November changelog also omits Website Advertising from its September 2025 entry, while the April capture listed it there. Neither omission gives an effective change date or account-specific treatment. Buyer-to-customer terminology, Markdown layout and the dispute-rate hyperlink are presentational or navigational. Keep the per-Product Dashboard/API code and Checkout Session or Payment Link scope, the US-sales qualification for the relevant business/personal rows, and Stripe's conditional rather than automatic 60-day refund authority (new raw lines 70-102, 117-120 and 201-209). Both captures exclude live in-person events, as the mapped summary correctly says. The proposed Managed Payments concept wording qualifies its broader live-event exclusion and points back to the exact audiovisual rows, which can cover digitally delivered live-event content (old raw lines 84-98, 149-151 and 172-174; new raw lines 84-98, 153-155 and 175-177). Check the delivery model, direct sale and distribution rights independently of the subject of the content. The general electronically supplied services code mentions minimal human involvement (old and new raw line 108). The separate fully automated requirement still excludes live human-delivered services. This distinction was present in both captures.

Managed Payments excludes physical goods, professional services, live in-person events, Connect platforms, Express accounts, and accounts controlled by a platform. Listed Digital Audio Visual Works codes can cover live-event content distributed as fully automated digital downloads, streams, or bundles. See [[source-stripe-managed-payments-eligibility]] for the specific code definitions.

For each eligible digital product, sell directly to customers, hold the necessary distribution rights and licences, and provide fully automated delivery. Live intervention such as one-to-one coaching disqualifies the service. If Stripe determines that a product is ineligible, the merchant must stop using Managed Payments for it and take responsibility for its indirect tax liability.
warnings: Both captures distinguish in-person events from digitally distributed live-event content. Consult the exact audiovisual rows and the separate product criteria.
